title: Only 7% Pass This Intelligence Test
summary: Patterns, number rules, word links, codes and spatial traps get harder across five fast challenges.

landing.intro: Patterns, codes, word links and logic traps collide in one fast intelligence challenge—how many can you solve?
landing.startNote: Short ad first - then it begins.

about.body:
This worldwide entertainment challenge mixes patterns, numerical rules, verbal connections, spatial reasoning, code-breaking, attention and logical deduction across 40 varied puzzles. It is designed to feel playful and increasingly demanding rather than like a formal aptitude exam.

Each puzzle has one answer supported by the information shown. The interaction changes regularly, so you may need to identify a rule, compare two clues, transform a symbol, calculate mentally or notice one tiny inconsistency.

Your Intelligence Test Score is simply the percentage of these entertainment puzzles you solve correctly. It describes this attempt only and does not measure your actual intelligence, IQ, aptitude or educational ability.

howToPlay.title: How to Play
steps: Solve each thinking challenge at your own pace—there is no timer or speed bonus.
Choose one answer per puzzle. Correctness remains hidden until the final reveal.
Keep going as the clues become harder, then reveal your score and complete answer review.

about.disclaimer: For entertainment and general learning only. This is not a standardised intelligence, IQ, aptitude, educational or psychological assessment.

profiles.title: The Systems Mastermind
profiles.copy: You consistently spotted hidden structure across very different types of problems. Patterns, constraints and small details tended to click into place quickly.

profiles.title: The Precision Thinker
profiles.copy: You combined strong rule detection with careful attention to detail. Even when the format changed, you usually found the important clue.

profiles.title: The Pattern Navigator
profiles.copy: You found your way through most of the vault by recognising how information connected. Your strongest moments came when there was a clear underlying rule to uncover.

profiles.title: The Adaptive Solver
profiles.copy: You handled a broad mix of challenges and adapted well when the puzzle style changed. Some locks opened instantly; others needed a different angle.

profiles.title: The Curious Analyst
profiles.copy: You cracked a solid share of the vault and kept experimenting when the rule was not immediately obvious. Your result shows a mixed reasoning profile rather than one dominant style.

profiles.title: The Creative Wildcard
profiles.copy: The vault caught you with some of its more structured rules, but you still found solutions across several challenge types. Your answers produced a lively and unpredictable reasoning pattern.

score.passed: You passed the Intelligence Test challenge!

details.analysisCopy: This 40-question result combines pattern spotting, number rules, word links, spatial transformations, attention and logical deduction. Each correct answer adds 2.5 percentage points.
details.roadmapIntro: Review the result to see which clue types clicked and where the closest traps appeared.
details.positionCopy: The entertainment target is 32 correct answers out of 40. Your marker shows how close this attempt came.
details.measuredIntro: The 40 puzzles span three broad forms of recreational problem-solving.

measuredAreas.title: Patterns and codes
measuredAreas.copy: Spotting sequences, inconsistencies and the rule hidden inside compact visual information.

measuredAreas.title: Words and numbers
measuredAreas.copy: Connecting language clues and applying visible numerical relationships accurately.

measuredAreas.title: Logic and space
measuredAreas.copy: Combining constraints, rotations and transformations to reach one supported conclusion.

details.tipsTitle: Three ways to sharpen your puzzle approach
details.tipsIntro: Simple ideas for a future attempt—not an intelligence or aptitude assessment.

tips.title: Name the rule
tips.copy: Before choosing, say the pattern or constraint in one short sentence.

tips.title: Check every clue
tips.copy: In logic puzzles, a small negative or condition often eliminates the tempting answer.

tips.title: Transform one step at a time
tips.copy: For rotations, mirrors and codes, apply each operation separately before comparing choices.

details.finalCopy: You solved {score} puzzles out of {total}. Your entertainment thinking profile for this attempt is shown below.

questions.question: Which symbol comes next?

visual.ariaLabel: circle, triangle, circle, triangle, unknown

questions.explanation: The symbols alternate circle, triangle, circle, triangle, so the next symbol is a circle.

questions.question: A square is 5 and a triangle is 3. What is triangle × square?

visual.ariaLabel: two squares equal ten; triangle plus square equals eight

questions.explanation: The triangle is 3 and the square is 5, so 3 × 5 = 15.

questions.question: Which word completes both phrases?

visual.ariaLabel: snow blank; blank room

questions.explanation: BALL completes both familiar phrases: snowball and ballroom.

questions.question: Which arrow is the reflection in a vertical mirror?

visual.ariaLabel: up-right arrow beside a vertical mirror

questions.explanation: A vertical mirror swaps left and right while preserving height, so up-right becomes up-left.

questions.question: Which copy contains a zero instead of the letter O?

visual.ariaLabel: four copies of LOCK; the third contains a zero

questions.explanation: The third copy is L0CK, using the digit zero instead of the letter O.

questions.question: All blue keys open Gate A. This key is blue. What must be true?
questions.explanation: The rule applies to every blue key, so this blue key must open Gate A.

questions.question: What comes next?

visual.ariaLabel: 2, 5, 8, 11, unknown

questions.explanation: The sequence increases by 3 each time: 2, 5, 8, 11, 14.

questions.question: Three boxes total 24. A holds 6 and B holds twice A. What does C hold?
questions.explanation: B holds 12. Subtracting 6 and 12 from 24 leaves 6 for C.

questions.question: The shapes gain one side each time. What comes next?

visual.ariaLabel: triangle, square, pentagon, unknown

questions.explanation: Triangle, square and pentagon have 3, 4 and 5 sides, so a hexagon with 6 sides comes next.

questions.question: The shifts repeat +1, +2, +1. How is DOG coded?

visual.ariaLabel: letter shifts plus one, plus two, plus one; CAT becomes DCU

questions.explanation: Apply +1, +2, +1: D becomes E, O becomes Q and G becomes H, producing EQH.

questions.question: You face north and turn right twice. Which way do you face?
questions.explanation: Two right turns make a half-turn, changing north to south.

questions.question: Which output breaks the displayed rule?

visual.ariaLabel: rule input times two plus one; two to five, three to seven, four to eight, five to eleven

questions.explanation: The rule is input × 2 + 1. Four should produce 9, not 8.

questions.question: All NIM are TOV. No TOV are RAK. Can any NIM be RAK?
questions.explanation: Every NIM is a TOV, and no TOV is a RAK, so no NIM can be a RAK.

questions.question: Each block is the sum of the two below it. What goes on top?

visual.ariaLabel: number pyramid with bottom 3, 5, 4 and middle 8, 9

questions.explanation: The middle blocks are 3 + 5 = 8 and 5 + 4 = 9. The top is 8 + 9 = 17.

questions.question: Bird is to nest as bee is to…
questions.explanation: A nest is a bird's home, while a hive is a bee's home.

questions.question: Which pair does not show a half-turn?
questions.explanation: Up and right differ by a quarter-turn, while every other pair differs by a half-turn.

questions.question: Mara is before Leo, and Leo is before Nia. Which order works?
questions.explanation: Mara must be first, Leo second and Nia third.

questions.question: A machine doubles a number, then adds 3. Which input produces 17?
questions.explanation: Subtract 3 from 17 to get 14, then divide by 2 to get 7.

questions.question: The first digit is colour; the second is shape. What code means blue square?

visual.ariaLabel: red equals one, blue equals two, triangle equals three, square equals four

questions.explanation: Blue is 2 and square is 4, so the colour-first code is 24.

questions.question: Which word appears immediately after BLUE?

visual.ariaLabel: red, blue, green, yellow

questions.explanation: GREEN appears directly after BLUE in the displayed sequence.

questions.question: Apply the same turn: if ↑ becomes ↘, what does ← become?

visual.ariaLabel: up becomes down-right; apply the same turn to left

questions.explanation: Up becomes down-right after a 135-degree clockwise turn. The same turn changes left to up-right.

questions.question: Which is the only option that is not a colour?
questions.explanation: Blue, amber and violet are colours; circle is a shape.

questions.question: What comes next?
questions.explanation: The increases double: +1, +2, +4, +8, then +16. Seventeen plus 16 is 33.

questions.question: Which two letters swapped position?

visual.ariaLabel: first sequence A B C D; second sequence A C B D

questions.explanation: Only B and C exchange places between the two sequences.

questions.question: Exactly one person tells the truth. A says B lies. B says C lies. C says A and B both lie. Who tells the truth?
questions.explanation: If B is truthful, C lies, A's claim is false and C's claim is false. That leaves exactly one truthful person.

questions.question: Which row breaks the two-part matching pattern?

visual.ariaLabel: four rows pairing a letter with its successor and a number with its double; the fourth skips a letter

questions.explanation: Each row should advance the letter by one and double the number. The fourth row skips from H to J.

questions.question: Which operation belongs in the gap?

visual.ariaLabel: six unknown operation three equals eighteen

questions.explanation: Six multiplied by three equals 18, so multiplication belongs in the gap.

questions.question: Start in the centre. Move up, right, right, then down. Where do you finish?

visual.ariaLabel: up, right, right, down

questions.explanation: The up and down moves cancel, leaving two moves to the right.

questions.question: Which word cannot naturally follow SUN?
questions.explanation: Sunlight, sunrise and sunset are familiar compounds; sunmoon is not.

questions.question: Which symbol completes the code?

visual.ariaLabel: triangle, circle, triangle, circle, unknown

questions.explanation: The symbols alternate triangle and circle, so the next symbol is a triangle.

questions.question: All glens are quiet. Some parks are glens. What must be true?
questions.explanation: The parks that are glens must also be quiet, so some parks are quiet.

questions.question: Which word completes both phrases?

visual.ariaLabel: time blank; blank work

questions.explanation: PIECE completes both familiar compounds: timepiece and piecework.

questions.question: Four vaults are W, X, Y and Z. It is not W or Z. If it were X, the alarm would be on. The alarm is off. Which vault is it?
questions.explanation: W and Z are ruled out. X would activate the alarm, but the alarm is off, so Y remains.

questions.question: In each row, double the first number, then add the second. What replaces the question mark?
questions.explanation: Double 7 to get 14, then add 3 to get 17.

questions.question: Two number patterns are interwoven. What replaces the question mark?
questions.explanation: The odd positions are 2, 3, 4, 5. The even positions are 8, 12, 16, 20.

questions.question: Start in the centre. Move up twice, right once, down once, then left twice. Where do you finish?

visual.ariaLabel: up, up, right, down, left, left

questions.explanation: The vertical moves leave one step up. The horizontal moves leave one step left.

questions.question: Swap only the first and last characters. Which code results?

visual.ariaLabel: code B7Q dash 4M2 dash K9

questions.explanation: The first character B and final character 9 exchange places; everything between them stays fixed.

questions.question: A machine runs every 3 days starting on day 2. On which day is its fourth run?
questions.explanation: The runs occur on days 2, 5, 8 and 11, so the fourth run is day 11.

questions.question: Both letter positions change by one each time. Which pair comes next?

visual.ariaLabel: A Z, B Y, C X, unknown

questions.explanation: The first letters move forward A, B, C, D while the second move backward Z, Y, X, W.

questions.question: An arrow points up. Turn it 90° clockwise, then reflect it in a vertical mirror. Where does it point?
questions.explanation: The clockwise turn makes the arrow point right. A vertical mirror changes right to left.
